business.name: Harbor & Vine Plumbing
business.what_they_do: Residential plumbing — drain cleaning, water heaters, repiping, slab leaks, sewer camera, emergency burst pipe

findings.title: Phone number is not a tappable tel: link
findings.evidence: automated_check: click_to_call — "A phone number appears as plain text ('(619) 555-0142') but is not a tel: link, so tapping it on a phone does nothing."
findings.confidence_reason: The check directly confirms the number exists as text but lacks the tel: protocol. Mobile users must memorize or copy-paste the number to call — a step many will not take.
findings.business_impact: Every mobile visitor who wants to call hits a dead tap. For an emergency plumber, this is the single biggest leak: the moment of highest intent (burst pipe, no hot water) is exactly when someone is on a phone and least willing to transcribe digits.
findings.fix: Wrap the number in (619) 555-0142 everywhere it appears — header, body, footer.

findings.title: No viewport meta tag — mobile renders as zoomed-out desktop
findings.evidence: automated_check: viewport_meta — "No viewport meta tag, so phones render the page at desktop width and zoom out."
findings.confidence_reason: The check is binary: the tag is absent. Without it, the 390px mobile viewport shows a 980px-wide page shrunk to fit, making the phone number, hours, and navigation tiny and unreadable without pinch-zoom.
findings.business_impact: Mobile visitors (likely >60% for local search) land on a page they cannot read. They leave before they even see the phone number. This compounds F1: even if the number were a link, it would be too small to hit reliably.

findings.title: All tap targets under 44×44px — navigation and CTAs too small for thumbs
findings.evidence: automated_check: tap_targets — "6 of 6 visible controls are under 44px, smallest 'Home' at 29x14px."
findings.confidence_reason: The check measured every visible interactive element. All six — the primary navigation — fail the 44px minimum. No manual testing needed to confirm the defect.
findings.business_impact: The 'Contact' link that passes cta_above_fold is geometrically present but physically untappable. A thumb covers the whole nav bar. Mis-taps send users to wrong pages or nowhere, increasing bounce before a call happens.
findings.fix: Increase padding/line-height on nav links and the Contact CTA to ≥44×44px. Use a mobile-first nav pattern (hamburger or stacked buttons) with generous hit areas.

findings.title: Stale "Site last updated March 2011" signal undermines trust for emergency work
findings.evidence: inference: Page text footer reads "Site last updated March 2011." Today is 2026-10-28 — over 15 years stale. Business context says "Serving San Diego since 1987" and "Emergency service available."
findings.confidence_reason: Would rise to high with a quick owner confirmation that the site content (services, hours, license) is current. The date itself is visible in the provided page text.
findings.business_impact: A homeowner with a burst pipe at 10 PM judges credibility in seconds. A 2011 timestamp suggests the business may be closed, the number dead, or the emergency promise empty. They call the next listing instead.
findings.fix: Remove the hard-coded "Site last updated" line or replace it with a dynamic "Content reviewed <current year>" if the info is current. Add a recent Google review or job photo with a 2024-2025 date.

findings.title: Title tag is only "Plumbing" (8 chars) and no meta description — weak search snippet
findings.evidence: automated_check: title_and_description — "title is only 8 characters; no meta description."
findings.confidence_reason: The check measures length and presence directly. DOM summary confirms title="Plumbing" and metaDescription="".
findings.business_impact: In Google Maps / local pack results, the snippet shows "Plumbing" with no descriptive line. Searchers see no location, no emergency hint, no "family owned since 1987." Click-through drops, so fewer people ever reach the page to call.
findings.fix: Title: "Harbor & Vine Plumbing | Emergency & Repiping | San Diego, CA" (≈60 chars). Meta description: "Family-owned since 1987. Licensed, bonded, insured. Drain cleaning, water heaters, slab leaks, 24/7 emergency. Call (619) 555-0142."

findings.title: 16 text elements below WCAG AA contrast — phone number and hours hard to read
findings.evidence: automated_check: text_contrast — "16 of 56 sampled text element(s) below WCAG AA. Worst is 2.13:1 where 4.5:1 is required ('Copyright 1998-2024 Harbor & Vine Plumbing. All rights reser')."
findings.confidence_reason: The check sampled 56 elements and computed contrast against opaque backgrounds. It cannot measure text over images/gradients (reported as unmeasurable). The worst offender is the copyright line, but body copy and the phone number may also be low-contrast.
findings.business_impact: Older homeowners (core plumbing demographic) struggle to read the number, hours, or address on a bright screen. They give up or mis-dial. The copyright line is the least important text but signals a systemic contrast problem.
findings.fix: Audit the color palette: ensure body text ≥4.5:1, large text (≥18px) ≥3:1. Darken gray body copy or lighten the background. Test the phone number line specifically.

findings.title: Broken heading structure (two H1s, jump to H3) — hurts screen-reader users and SEO
findings.evidence: automated_check: heading_structure — "Heading outline is broken: 2 h1 elements; h1 is followed by h3." DOM summary shows H1: "Harbor & Vine Plumbing", H1: "Welcome To Our Website", then H3: "Our Services", "What Our Customers Say", "Contact Us".
findings.confidence_reason: The check and DOM summary agree on the exact heading tree. No ambiguity.
findings.business_impact: Screen-reader users (some of whom are homeowners with disabilities) cannot navigate by heading hierarchy. Google may misunderstand page topic. Indirectly reduces calls from accessibility-reliant users and organic search.
findings.fix: Single H1: "Harbor & Vine Plumbing — San Diego Plumbing Since 1987". H2 for major sections: "Our Services", "What Our Customers Say", "Contact Us". Remove the second H1.

findings.title: Two images have no alt text — minor accessibility gap
findings.evidence: automated_check: image_alt_text — "2 of 2 visible image(s) have no alt text (e.g. gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAMLCwgAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA, gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAMLCwgAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA)."
findings.confidence_reason: The check found two base64-encoded GIFs (likely spacers or tracking pixels) with empty alt. Presence/emptiness is binary.
findings.business_impact: Negligible for calls. Only matters if images convey content (badges, license photos, truck wrap). These appear to be decorative/spacers.
findings.fix: Add alt="" to decorative images. If either image is a trust badge (license, BBB, manufacturer), add descriptive alt text.

overall.verdict: The site has strong trust signals (35+ years, family-owned, licensed, testimonials) but three mobile-first technical failures — no tel: link, no viewport meta, undersized tap targets — block the majority of high-intent mobile visitors from calling. A stale 2011 timestamp erodes the trust the copy builds. Fix the top three and update the date; the rest are polish.
overall.biggest_opportunity: Add tel: links and the viewport tag today. That alone makes the existing traffic callable on mobile.
overall.redesign_brief: Lead with the phone number as a prominent, tappable button in a sticky header: "Call (619) 555-0142 — 24/7 Emergency". Prove with the two testimonials, the 1987 start date, and the license/bonded/insured line — all above the fold. Cut the "Welcome To Our Website" H1, the 2011 timestamp, the base64 spacer images, and the gray-on-gray copyright line. Make the nav a mobile-first stack of three fat buttons: Call, Services, Contact. Ensure every text element hits 4.5:1 contrast. Title and meta description must sell the click in search results.

sections.name: Technical / Accessibility Implementation Notes
sections.purpose: Answer F2, F3, F6, F8 — the non-content fixes that make the content usable.
sections.content_notes: Add <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'> (F2). All interactive elements (nav links, CTA buttons, tel links) minimum 44×44px with generous padding (F3). Full color audit: body text ≥4.5:1, large text (≥18px) ≥3:1 — darken gray copy or lighten background; test phone number line specifically (F6). Two base64 GIFs: add alt='' if decorative; if either is a trust badge (license, BBB, manufacturer), add descriptive alt (F8). Single H1, then H2s only (F7). Page weight <600KB, first render <2s on cold 4G.

BBB rating, Angie's List, HomeAdvisor or other third-party badges

plan.design_direction: Mobile-first, high-contrast, utilitarian. Sticky header with fat call button. Three-button mobile nav stack: Call | Services | Contact. No gradients, no hero images, no animations, no chat widgets. Type scale: H1 ~28px, H2 ~22px, body ~18px, all ≥4.5:1 contrast. Color palette: navy/white/amber accent — trust colors, not marketing colors. Photos only if real: Ray Vine, truck wrap, job site (slab leak, water heater) with 2024-2025 EXIF dates. No stock photography.

draft.subject: Phone link not tappable
draft.body:
Subject: Phone link not tappable

Hi,

Your phone number is not a tappable tel: link (F1). It also lacks a viewport meta tag (F2) and the contact button is too small for thumbs (F3).

Every mobile visitor who wants to call hits a dead tap. That lost call can mean a missed emergency job, which costs you revenue.

Check this - I rebuilt your page so you can look at it instead of imagining it: http://localhost:3000/mockup/demo-harbor-vine-plumbing-example

That page is a concept mockup I made, not affiliated with Harbor & Vine Plumbing. It passed 11 of 13 automated checks, against 3 of 13 for the current page.

Please look at the page I already built and reply yes or no.

Best,

Sam Reyes - 1234 Example St, Suite 100, San Diego, CA 92101
You are receiving this one-off note because your business is listed publicly in San Diego, CA.
Reply "unsubscribe" and I will remove you and never contact you again.
